subject: AI & Agents
title: Features: What the Model Actually Sees
description: A quick, practical guide to Features: What the Model Actually Sees.

hook.text: A house-price model doesn't know about 'charming kitchens.' It sees: bedrooms=3, sqft=1400, zip=90210.

buildup.text: Features are the measurable properties you feed into a model — the raw inputs.

discovery.text: Good features make learning easy. Bad features make even the best algorithm fail.

twist.text: Feature engineering — choosing and crafting the right inputs — was once 80% of an ML engineer's job.

climax.text: Deep learning changed this by learning features automatically from raw data.

punchline.text: What you feed in matters more than the algorithm you choose.

quiz.question: What are features in machine learning?
options: Measurable input properties fed to the model

details.summary: Features are the measurable properties that a model uses as input — pixel values, word frequencies, sensor readings. Choosing the right features determines whether the model can learn meaningful patterns.
details.whyItMatters: Feature selection is often more important than algorithm choice. The best model in the world cannot learn if it never sees the relevant information. Features define what AI can and cannot discover.
takeaways: Features are the measurable inputs a model processes
Choosing relevant features is critical for model success
Deep learning automates feature discovery from raw data

faq.question: What is the difference between features and data?
faq.answer: Data is raw information like images or text. Features are specific measurable properties extracted from that data — like edge counts in an image or word frequencies in text — that the model actually uses for learning.

faq.question: Do modern AI models still need manual feature engineering?
faq.answer: Deep learning models automatically discover features from raw data. However, for traditional ML methods on structured data, manual feature engineering remains important and often determines model performance.
